instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Ten goals and eleven assists in the Keegan side: his best season by some distance.
Rows at both Everton and Fulham in the same season; the same player at each.
Rows at both Everton and Fulham in the same season; the same player at each.
Thirty-four, five starts, and in his last season as a top-flight footballer.
An ever-present and Spurs’ outstanding performer in an otherwise ordinary season.
Thirty-seven and first choice for the second half of Fulham’s escape; still a sound handler, no longer quick to his feet.

Twenty, seven league goals from left-back, and one of the outstanding debut seasons of the year in a Liverpool side that finished second; the athleticism and the left foot were already top-flight weapons.
Thirty-five and third-choice cover at Fulham.

Joined Coventry in February 1995.

Three further Coventry starts before the Southampton move; the same player at both.
Twenty-three goals at 32 and still Arsenal's most dangerous player.
Thirty-four, at West Ham, and moving noticeably worse.
Rated as the raw, wasteful teenager he was at Arsenal, not the Fulham player of 2005.
Nine goals from the left at 25 - the season the pace and directness finally came with an end product.
Split between Fulham and West Ham in January; the same player at both, and one league goal at either.
Split between Fulham and West Ham in January; the same player at both, and one league goal at either.
Season ended by a cruciate injury in November.
The aerial focal point of the Quinn/Phillips partnership in a side that finished seventh; his most effective top-flight season, at 32.
Thirty-four and in his last season; still a useful aerial reference point but no longer able to lead a line.
Broke into a treble-winning defence at 18; rated as the promising teenager he was, not the England international he became.
Thirty-four starts at right-back in a side that won the league conceding 22 and the European Cup; the best season of his career.
Player-manager of a relegated side; still England-standard defensively but stretched by the job and by his age.
Thirty-seven and a squad player, though still an outstanding striker of a dead ball.
Thirty-eight years old and still a thirty-four-start regular. The appearances are remarkable; the footballer is a squad-standard defender living on reading and dead balls.
Season broken up by a prison sentence and a hernia operation.
The most dominant aerial centre-forward in the division; neither the rest of his game nor his availability ever matched it.
Nine starts, six goals — the availability problem that defined the second half of his career.
Six starts at 32 and used almost entirely as a substitute battering ram.
Seven starts and one goal at 33; a substitute battering ram and no longer able to start.
A composed, left-footed ball-playing centre-half in a relegated side; the move to Celtic and a long Everton career reflect the ability on show here.
Six years on from Bolton - Celtic, and a testicular cancer diagnosis and recovery, in between; the same composed left-footed defender, a little more experienced and a little slower.
A central defender in an Everton side that finished fourth conceding 46; solid and well organised rather than newly elite.
A season split between Sunderland and Everton after a summer move and a January return; the same player at both.
A season split between Sunderland and Everton after a summer move and a January return; the same player at both.
Thirty-five and split between Derby and Everton; the same player at both.
Thirty-five and split between Derby and Everton; the same player at both.
Seven goals from centre-back, almost all headers. The AerialThreat role is the whole of his attacking game and is meant literally.
Thirty-two and relegated; the aerial game was intact but he was being turned.
Three starts at 34, effectively at the end of his career.
Charlton’s first-choice keeper on their return to the top flight and a Republic of Ireland international; consistent and well positioned, no more than that.
An ever-present for a Charlton side that finished seventh; the best season of his career.
Split between Charlton and Portsmouth; the same keeper at both.
Split between Charlton and Portsmouth; the same keeper at both.
Three starts at 37 as emergency cover.
Six goals and an England cap at 23; as good as he got.
Cruciate damage; twelve starts, and he lost a yard he never recovered.
Three starts — knee trouble had reduced him to a fringe forward.
No goals in a title-winning season, which is the role rather than a failing: the delivery for Shearer and Sutton is the contribution.
Five starts; a knee problem cost him most of the year and much of his pace.
Twelve league goals from the right in a Double season and the Football Writers’ pick; elite, and the equal of his Invincibles year rather than a peak above it.
Four seasons of development on from 1999/00: by the Invincibles year he was an elite wide forward, timing runs beyond the front line rather than holding the touchline.
One league goal in twenty-one starts: hip trouble and a run of migraines took the timing out of his runs, and he was never the same player afterwards.
Two league goals in a season badly disrupted by injury; the pace and movement were still top-flight.
Split between City and Charlton around an eight-match ban for the elbow on Pedro Mendes; the same player at both.
Split between City and Charlton around an eight-match ban for the elbow on Pedro Mendes; the same player at both.
Ever-present and the metronome of an Ipswich side that finished fifth; genuinely good at the unglamorous parts, never near elite.
Three starts at 41.

Eighteen, and already an outstanding one-v-one dribbler with a genuine end product some of the time; not yet the finisher or decision-maker. Rated as the player that season, well below the 90s he reached from 2006/07.
More consistent and physically stronger, still wasteful. Good rather than elite.
Twenty, nine league goals, and the end product arriving often enough to make the dribbling decisive.
Seventeen goals from wide, PFA Player of the Year and a title. The season he stopped being a winger who crossed and became a wide forward who scored, which is why the trait changes here.
Thirty-one league goals from wide, a Ballon d’Or and a European Cup. An all-time great season, alongside Henry 2003/04 rather than beneath it.
Twenty-six league goals in twenty-eight starts in a first season in Spain, interrupted by an ankle injury.
Two seasons on from the previous row: he went from a teenage squad option to the most dangerous attacker at City.
A British record fee and ten starts; used sparingly by Mourinho and visibly less certain of himself than at City.
Eighteen, six starts, a squad teenager rather than a Premier League footballer yet.

A season out of the top flight in between; six starts at 30 and effectively finished.
Moved to Bolton in January; the same player at both clubs.
Moved to Bolton in January; the same player at both clubs.
Thirty-one and the passing hub of the Ipswich side that finished fifth; his best top-flight season.
A modern-era specialist defensive full-back with no attacking game at all; by 31 a rotation option rather than a starter.
Relegated with Coventry; a limited centre-half whom the division had moved past.
Seven starts at 32 after a season in Malaysia.
Thirteen goals at 34; a limited but genuinely effective penalty-box striker to the end.
His best season: a good passer for a centre-half of that era, and Liverpool's first choice.
Fitness and weight problems cost him the place, and a good deal of the ability with it.
Thirty-five starts at twenty in Wigan’s first top-flight season; the left foot and the delivery were already the best part of him.
A first Everton season spent behind Lescott; thirteen starts, and no worse a footballer for it.
Thirty-seven starts and eight assists at twenty-four; Everton’s settled first choice and among the better attacking left-backs in the division.
His peak season: the best left-back in the league that year on delivery and set pieces, if never dominant defensively.
African Footballer of the Year in each of the two years before this and a World Cup quarter-finalist; three league goals is a poor return, but the ability was real.
Split between Blackburn and Sunderland; the same player at both.
Split between Blackburn and Sunderland; the same player at both.
Thirty-six and at Sunderland, still a competent starter.
Eight goals from midfield for Sunderland after a record fee; his most productive season.

Fifteen goals conceded in 35 games and a record clean-sheet run. Positioning, handling and shot-stopping were all at the very top of the world game that season, which is what puts him in the 90s at 22 rather than the 80s.
The fractured skull at Reading in October cost him three months and, on the evidence of everything after it, a little of the command that had made him unbeatable at twenty-two.
Thirty-four starts in a Double-winning season and back close to his best, though not back to the 2004/05 level.
Still Liverpool’s best player, but slower since the 1991 Achilles rupture.
Reinvented as a central midfielder after the Achilles injury and very good at it; the pace was gone, the football was not.
Two starts at 34 for Charlton.
Eleven assists from wide in a first English season; an Australia regular and a Champions League player with Feyenoord, athletic and two-footed.
